Title: Create a new urgent order with delivery date and verify urgency flag is set in response
Preconditions: A shop with ID 1 exists, and an item with ID 1 exists in the system
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"status": "success", "message": "Order created successfully", "data": {"urgent": true, "items": [{"measurementGroups": [{"urgent": true, "deliveryDate": "2023-12-20"}]}]}}

Title: Create a new non-urgent order without delivery date and verify urgency flag is not set in response
Preconditions: A shop with ID 1 exists, and an item with ID 1 exists in the system
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"status": "success", "message": "Order created successfully", "data": {"urgent": false, "items": [{"measurementGroups": [{"urgent": false, "deliveryDate": null}]}]}}

Title: Verify that order item status update response does not expose sensitive system details in success messages
Section: Order Management - Order Item Status Update
Preconditions: An existing order item with ID 1 exists. User is authenticated and authorized to update the order item status.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing 'status: success', 'message: Order status updated successfully.', and no sensitive system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors) in any field.

Title: Verify that the urgent flag is correctly exposed in order summary responses for authorized users
Preconditions: An existing order with ID 1 exists and has 'urgent' set to true. User is authenticated and authorized to view the order.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1. 2. Observe the response body for the 'urgent' field.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing 'status: success' and the order details, including 'urgent: true' in the response data. No sensitive system details are exposed.

Title: Verify that the urgent flag is correctly exposed in paginated order summary responses for authorized users
Section: Order Management - Urgent Flag Exposure in Order Summary
Preconditions: At least one order exists for the shop with ID 1 and has 'urgent' set to true. User is authenticated and authorized to view the shop's orders.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/1?page=0&limit=10. 2. Observe the response body for the 'urgent' field in the order summaries.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing 'status: success' and a list of orders, each including the 'urgent' field with the correct boolean value. No sensitive system details are exposed.

Title: Verify that the urgent flag cannot be manipulated via mass assignment in order creation
Section: Order Management - Urgent Flag Mass Assignment
Preconditions: User is authenticated and authorized to create orders for the shop.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders with the payload in testData, including an unexpected 'isUrgent' field. 2. Observe the response and the created order's urgent flag.

Test Data: {
  "customerName": "John Doe",
  "customerPhone": "1234567890",
  "customerGender": "MALE",
  "orderGender": "MALE",
  "customerPhotoUrl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",
  "totalAmount": 1000,
  "paidAmount": 500,
  "dueAmount": 500,
  "trialDate": "2023-12-01",
  "orderDate": "2023-11-01",
  "deliveryDate": "2023-12-15",
  "urgent": false,
  "isUrgent": true,
  "items": [
    {
      "itemId": 1,
      "quantity": 1,
      "measurementGroups": [
        {
          "photoUrl": "http://example.com/photo.jpg",
          "urgent": false,
          "measurements": [
            {
              "nameEn": "Chest",
              "nameBn": "বুক",
              "unit": "cm",
              "value": 90
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "shopId": 1
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and creates the order with 'urgent: false', ignoring the injected 'isUrgent' field. The response body reflects the correct urgent flag status.
